audit.method: Read from the full term sheet by one AI reviewer, then checked against it twice by independent AI reviewers: first every line of the record against the document, then the document section by section against the record. Not signed off by a person. Every quote is looked up in the PDF text each time the tool runs.
audit.open_points:
Final record: C:\Users\AFarid\Documents\Hackathon\key_credit_terms\data\audited\honeywell_364day_2026.json. Checker: structure OK, 61 quotes exact, none loose, missing or on another page. A programmatic diff against the first-audit record shows only the two changes listed; no printed line, status or evidence quote changed.

Reverse pass (document to record): every section on pages 1-10 was mapped to a template row or confirmed to have none. No term was found missing from a row, in the wrong row, or carrying a figure from the wrong place; the document has a single facility and no existing / proposed columns. Every number in the record was confirmed against the dump, and pages 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 10 against the page images. Searches of the dump for accordion, guarantee, Barclays, jurisdiction, reporting periods, budget, conditions subsequent, letters of credit / swingline, financial ratios and ranking found nothing that would upgrade a not_stated or by_reference row.

What the term sheet itself cannot resolve:
1. Financial covenants: none is among the twelve covenants listed, but the list is 'including, but not limited to' and defers to the Existing 364-Day Agreement. Under the open-list rule the four fc_* rows and the unlisted permitted_* rows stay by_reference; whether the facility has a financial covenant has to come from the credit agreement.
2. Guarantors: no guarantee provision and the Company is the only obligor named, but the term sheet never says the facility is unguaranteed, so the row stays not_stated rather than 'None'.
3. Change of Control: each Lender may terminate its commitment (10 days' notice, effective 60 days after); the term sheet is silent on repayment of that Lender's Advances. The printed line says so.
4. 'Spin Off' and 'Voting Stock' are used as defined terms but not defined. The Spin Off is cross-referenced in the Permitted Disposals row as 'contemplated' only; the term sheet does not say what it is or that any covenant permits it.
5. Three-quote limit: bankruptcy/insolvency, the $500m ERISA threshold and the 'Debt' definition (page 7), participations and 'to any of its affiliates' (page 8), and 'increments of $1,000,000' in the prepayment sentence are stated in the lines and verified against the dump but not quoted. I tested re-cuts: covering the page 7 items would mean dropping the quote for the payment grace periods, so no arrangement of three quotes covers everything.
6. Six lines exceed the 250-character soft target (longest 407, hard limit 420); shortening them would drop conditions.
7. Barclays is not named; it may be among the 'other financial institutions'. No lender commitments are stated.
8. No date is printed on the document (footer '2026 Honeywell Term Sheet' only), so doc.date is empty.
9. Default interest, Majority Lenders, the Company's lender replacement rights, borrowing mechanics and pricing have no template row and are in notes only.

doc.title: Honeywell International Inc. - Summary of Terms and Conditions - $3,000,000,000 364-Day Multi-Currency Revolving Credit Facility
doc.notes: Indicative Summary of Terms and Conditions sent to prospective lenders for a new $3.0bn 364-day unsecured multi-currency revolving credit facility for Honeywell International Inc.; no date is printed (the footer reads '2026 Honeywell Term Sheet'). The terms are on pages 1-9 in a label / value layout and page 10 is the 364-Day Pricing Grid (ratings-based commitment fee and margin). It is not an amendment and has no existing / proposed columns: it is a new facility, with termination of commitments under the Existing 364-Day Credit Agreement dated as of March 17, 2025 as a condition precedent to closing. Conditions precedent, representations, covenants and events of default are given as open lists ('including, but not limited to') that otherwise defer to the Existing 364-Day Agreement, so no financial covenants, baskets or reporting periods are set out; a companion 5-Year Facility is mentioned but not described. Pricing is shown but has no row in the template: across the six ratings levels of the grid (page 10) the Commitment Fee is 0.02% to 0.09% and the Applicable Margin for Term SOFR and EURIBOR Advances is 0.50% to 1.125% (Base Rate Advances 100 basis points lower, but not less than 0.00%; page 3).
